api/Axiam.Sdk.AspNetCore.AxiamAuthMiddle.summary: Class AxiamAuthMiddleware Namespace Axiam.Sdk.AspNetCore Assembly Axiam.Sdk.AspNetCore.dll ASP.NET Core authentication middleware (D-06, CONTRACT.md §10 "ASP.NET Core" row: app.UseMiddleware<AxiamAuthMiddleware>() in Program.cs). Mirrors sdks/java/.../spring/AxiamAuthenticationFilter.java's authoritative sequence (extract → verify → exp-check → cross-tenant-check → inject-identity → 401 JSON on failure), adapted to ASP.NET Core's ClaimsPrincipal/User integration point — the direct analog of Java D-14's Spring SecurityContext integration. public sealed class AxiamAuthMiddleware Inheritance object AxiamAuthMiddleware Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Security-critical invariants (T-21-17, T-21-19, T-21-20): When NO credential is presented at all, the request is passed through unauthenticated — the framework's own [Authorize]/authorization middleware 401s it (via AxiamAuthorizationMiddlewareResultHandler, registered by AddAxiamAspNetCore(IServiceCollection, Action<AxiamOptions>)). This middleware never rejects a request for the mere absence of a token (Java filter lines 78-83 precedent) — doing so would incorrectly 401 public/anonymous endpoints that never carry a token at all. When a token IS presented, it is verified via the shared AxiamClient's internal JwksVerifier local fast path: alg-pinned Ed25519 signature check, THEN the mandatory post-signature tenant_id claim check (Pitfall 3 — the JWKS document is organization-wide, not tenant-scoped, so signature validity alone never implies tenant authorization). An explicit exp re-check is performed here too as defense in depth, mirroring the Java filter's lines 88-91 even though JwksVerifier.VerifyAsync already checks exp internally. User is rebuilt from scratch on every request from a fresh VerifyAsync call — it is NEVER cached beyond the current request, and never beyond the token's own remaining TTL (§10). Every failure path writes a standardized JSON body via WriteAsJsonAsync<TValue>(HttpResponse, TValue, CancellationToken) (System.Text.Json) — never manual string concatenation, so a message containing quotes/control characters can never produce malformed or injected JSON (PATTERNS.md "Standardized JSON error body"). CSRF (cookie double-submit, CONTRACT.md §3): when the credential was sourced from the axiam_access COOKIE (not the Authorization header) and the request method is state-changing (anything other than GET/HEAD/OPTIONS), this middleware additionally requires the X-CSRF-Token request header to be present and equal (constant-time, FixedTimeEquals(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, ReadOnlySpan<byte>)) to the axiam_csrf cookie value, rejecting with 403 on mismatch/absence. Bearer-header requests are CSRF-immune by construction — a cross-site attacker cannot set arbitrary request headers — but a cookie automatically attached by the browser is not, and in any same-site deployment where axiam_access reaches this app, the non-httpOnly axiam_csrf cookie does too. This mirrors, locally, the same double-submit check the AXIAM server performs on its own endpoints (§3). Constructors AxiamAuthMiddleware(RequestDelegate) Constructs the middleware. Registered by the ASP.NET Core pipeline (app.UseMiddleware<AxiamAuthMiddleware>()), which supplies next. public AxiamAuthMiddleware(RequestDelegate next) Parameters next RequestDelegate The next delegate in the middleware pipeline. api/Axiam.Sdk.AspNetCore.AxiamAuthorizat.summary: Class AxiamAuthorizationMiddlewareResultHandler Namespace Axiam.Sdk.AspNetCore Assembly Axiam.Sdk.AspNetCore.dll Custom IAuthorizationMiddlewareResultHandler that writes the standardized JSON error body (CONTRACT.md §10/§11, PATTERNS.md "Standardized JSON error body") for every authorization outcome: an unauthenticated result (401), a "lacks permission" result (403 — AxiamPolicyHandler left an AxiamRequirement unsatisfied, i.e. AuthzError), an unresolvable resource id (400 invalid_request, CONTRACT.md §11.2.3), and a transport failure while checking access (503 authz_unavailable, fail-closed per CONTRACT.md §11.2.5). On success, the pipeline continues exactly like the framework default. public sealed class AxiamAuthorizationMiddlewareResultHandler : IAuthorizationMiddlewareResultHandler Inheritance object AxiamAuthorizationMiddlewareResultHandler Implements IAuthorizationMiddlewareResultHandler Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks This handler deliberately does NOT branch on Forbidden/Challenged. Neither this package nor a typical consumer registers an ASP.NET Core authentication scheme (AddAuthentication()/UseAuthentication()) — identity comes entirely from AxiamAuthMiddleware setting User directly. Because of that, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization.Policy.PolicyEvaluator's internal authentication step always resolves to AuthenticateResult.NoResult() (Succeeded == false) since the evaluated policy carries no AuthenticationSchemes — which means EVERY non-success outcome, including an authenticated-but-forbidden one, would surface as Challenged, never Forbidden. Branching on User's own Identity.IsAuthenticated instead sidesteps that ambiguity entirely and is the authoritative signal: AxiamAuthMiddleware is the only code path that ever sets an authenticated identity, and it only does so after JwksVerifier signature+tenant verification succeeds. Absent either signal, falls back to the §10 behavior: 403 (authorization_denied) when User is already authenticated (an AxiamRequirement was left unsatisfied by AxiamPolicyHandler), otherwise 401 (authentication_failed). api/Axiam.Sdk.Auth.JwksVerifier.html.summary: Class JwksVerifier Namespace Axiam.Sdk.Auth Assembly Axiam.Sdk.dll Local EdDSA (Ed25519) JWKS verification (D-02, CONTRACT.md §10 local-verification fast path). .NET has no native Ed25519/EdDSA support anywhere in System.Security.Cryptography (confirmed research finding — dotnet/runtime #14741/#63174 remain unimplemented through .NET 10 GA), so this class uses BouncyCastle.Cryptography's Org.BouncyCastle.Crypto.Signers.Ed25519Signer / Org.BouncyCastle.Crypto.Parameters.Ed25519PublicKeyParameters directly — the single, well-vetted, verify-only crypto dependency D-02 permits. public sealed class JwksVerifier Inheritance object JwksVerifier Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks VerifyAsync(string, string, CancellationToken) applies the COMPLETE CONTRACT.md §10.1 "minimum local-verification set", every rule of which fails closed. This SDK uses NO JWT library: there is no System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt, JwtSecurityTokenHandler or TokenValidationParameters anywhere in the dependency graph (.NET ships no Ed25519 primitive, so the JOSE processing is hand-rolled over BouncyCastle). Every rule below is therefore enforced explicitly here rather than delegated to a library whose defaults would need auditing. signature — alg is pinned to "EdDSA" and checked BEFORE any key (kid) lookup, so alg: none and HS-family confusion are rejected without ever consulting a key. The token's own header never selects its verifier. exp — REQUIRED. A token carrying no exp, or an exp that is not a JSON number, is rejected. An absent exp is a *permanent credential*, never "no expiry constraint" — treating it as the latter is the SEC-080 defect. nbf — honoured when present; an nbf in the future is rejected. An absent nbf is valid. tenant_id — REQUIRED and asserted against the caller-supplied expected tenant, AFTER signature verification succeeds. An absent claim, or an empty expected tenant, fails closed. The JWKS document is organization-wide, not tenant-scoped, so a valid signature alone never implies tenant authorization (Pitfall 3 — independently confirmed by every sibling SDK). iss — checked only when this verifier was constructed with an expected issuer (see ExpectedIssuer). Unset by default. aud — checked only when this verifier was constructed with an expected audience (see ExpectedAudience). Unset by default. Accepts the single-string and array forms RFC 7519 permits. clock skew — ClockSkewLeeway, a named 60-second constant applied to rules 2 and 3. It is deliberately NOT operator-configurable. VerifyAsync(string, string, CancellationToken) NEVER throws for attacker-controlled input — every failure mode (bad alg, unknown kid, tampered/invalid signature, wrong tenant, missing/expired/ non-numeric exp, future nbf, issuer/audience mismatch, malformed/ non-base64/truncated token) returns null. This matches the AMQP HMAC verifier's fail-closed convention (Amqp/Hmac.cs). Verifies a webhook delivery's X-Axiam-Signature header against body and returns the parsed WebhookEvent on success. public static WebhookEvent Verify(Sensitive<string> secret, string signatureHeader, ReadOnlySpan<byte> body, TimeSpan? tolerance = null, TimeProvider? timeProvider = null) Parameters secret Sensitive<string> The webhook's plaintext signing secret (CONTRACT.md §7 Sensitive<T>). Its raw UTF-8 bytes are the HMAC key. Wrap a bare string with Wrap(T). signatureHeader string The raw, unparsed X-Axiam-Signature header value — t=<unix_seconds>,v1=<hex>, optionally with multiple v1 entries during secret rotation. body ReadOnlySpan<byte> The exact raw bytes received off the wire, before any JSON parsing. Re-serializing a parsed body (different key order/whitespace) changes these bytes and breaks the MAC — callers MUST buffer and pass the untouched request body. In ASP.NET Core this means enabling HttpRequest.EnableBuffering() (or reading the body stream directly) before any model binder has had a chance to parse and re-serialize it. tolerance TimeSpan? The freshness window; null or a non-positive value falls back to DefaultTolerance (300 seconds). Rejects a t= more than this far in the past OR the future — a two-sided check, so a future-dated timestamp is rejected just like a stale one (clock-skew abuse). timeProvider TimeProvider Test/injection seam for "now"; defaults to System. Pass a fake TimeProvider to deterministically exercise the freshness check. Returns WebhookEvent The verified, parsed WebhookEvent. Exceptions WebhookVerificationException The header is malformed (no v1, more than one t, non-numeric t, or empty), no supplied v1 matches the recomputed MAC, or t falls outside the freshness tolerance. The exception message is always a fixed, generic reason string — never the expected signature or the secret (CONTRACT.md §13.3 rule 6).

index.html.summary: AXIAM .NET SDK API reference for the AXIAM .NET packages: Axiam.Sdk — the client: cookie-session authentication (LoginAsync, VerifyMfaAsync, RefreshAsync, LogoutAsync), authorization (CheckAccessAsync, BatchCheckAsync), the gRPC authorization client, the OIDC/SSO relying-party helpers (OidcDiscoverAsync, OidcBegin, OidcExchangeAsync, OidcRefreshAsync, LoginClientCredentialsAsync, IntrospectAsync, RevokeAsync, SsoStartAsync, SsoCompleteAsync), and the AMQP consumer with HMAC verification and replay protection. Axiam.Sdk.AspNetCore — the resource-server middleware for ASP.NET Core: verifies the AXIAM JWT locally against a cached JWKS, enforces the cross-tenant claim check, applies the CSRF double-submit check to cookie-authenticated state-changing requests, and wires the "Login with AXIAM" OIDC login/callback endpoints (MapAxiamOidcLogin). See the AXIAM SDK contract for the behaviour every AXIAM SDK guarantees.
